key_insight: Foundational-NCA uses genetic prompting to adapt a 211,000-parameter model to medical segmentation tasks without retraining.
clinical_relevance: Its compact size could help make medical image segmentation more accessible in resource-limited settings, though clinical utility remains unproven.
method: Combines gradient-based learning with genetic optimization over a latent task space.
Uses a compact task vector to guide segmentation predictions.
evidence_signal: On TotalSegmentator, evaluation across 15 trained and 6 entirely unseen segmentation tasks yielded average Dice scores of 84.5% and 60.4%, respectively.
watch_item: Lower performance on unseen tasks highlights a generalization gap; small parameter count alone does not establish clinical readiness or deployment efficiency.
paper_title: A 211K Parameter Foundation Model: Genetic Prompting in Neural Cellular Automata
